name: Wrocław
tagline: A city of a hundred bridges on the Oder, with a colourful market square, a cathedral island and hundreds of tiny bronze gnomes hiding in the streets.
highlight: Hunting for the city's little bronze gnomes across the colourful Market Square.
shortDescription: A lively riverside city with a pastel Market Square, Ostrów Tumski cathedral island, the UNESCO-listed Centennial Hall, the Racławice Panorama and a trail of gnome statues.
metaDescription: A Wrocław travel guide: the Market Square, Ostrów Tumski, Centennial Hall, the gnome trail, Racławice Panorama, Cathedral Island, food, where to stay, how to get there and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Market Square, bridges, gnomes, student life

image.alt: Colourful townhouses on the Market Square in Wrocław

intro: Wrocław is Poland's fourth-largest city, on the Oder river in the south-west, and it has been Bohemian, Austrian, Prussian and German (as Breslau) before becoming Polish after 1945. That layered past shows in its architecture. The Market Square, one of the largest in Poland, is surrounded by pastel gabled houses and a Gothic town hall, and behind it run cobbled streets and canals.

The city is built on islands and riverbanks, with about 100 bridges. Ostrów Tumski, the oldest part, is a quiet island of churches, gas lamps and a cathedral with two tall spires, and a lit-lantern-lighting ceremony each evening. South-east of the centre, the Centennial Hall, a pioneering concrete dome of 1913, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Wrocław is also playful. Hundreds of small bronze gnomes hide around the streets, a legacy of a 1980s anti-communist art protest, and hunting for them is a popular activity. As a university city, it has lively bars, and it was European Capital of Culture in 2016. Two days is enough for the highlights.
